items.title: ApostropheCMS import-export tar guard misses './..' because it is a literal '../' substring test
items.summary: ### Summary The tar-extraction guard added to `@apostrophecms/import-export` for GHSA-mwxc-m426-3f78 is a literal substring test for `../`, and `./..` does not contain that substring. An entry named `./..` therefore passes the guard, `path.join` normalizes it to the parent of the export directory, and the resulting `fs.WriteStream` opens a directory and emits `EISDIR` with no `error` listener attached, which terminates the Node process. items.title: ApostropheCMS: Path traversal in uploadfs
items.summary: ## Summary The `uploadfs` library's local storage backend does not validate or sanitize user-supplied paths. The `prefixPath()` helper only strips double slashes (`//`) and the backend performs direct string concatenation (`uploadsPath + path`). items.title: ApostropheCMS: Authenticated Object-Level Authorization Bypass in exist-in-locale Reveals Restricted Localized Draft Identifiers
items.summary: **Summary** ApostropheCMS’s exist-in-locale API allows an authenticated low-privilege user to determine whether restricted documents exist in a specified locale and mode, including draft mode. The endpoint returns localized document identifiers without applying document-level view or edit authorization criteria. The issue was reproduced against a real local ApostropheCMS application running the reviewed source code. The test used a synthetic guest account and synthetic restricted draft records.

items.title: ApostropheCMS: Client-side Prototype Pollution in apos.http.parseQuery leading to DOM-based XSS against authenticated users
items.summary: ## Summary The client-side helper `apos.http.parseQuery()` in ApostropheCMS builds a nested object from a URL query string without sanitizing the keys `__proto__`, `constructor`, or `prototype`. Parsing an attacker-controlled query string therefore writes arbitrary properties onto `Object.prototype` (client-side prototype pollution). items.title: ApostropheCMS: Host header controls server-side image fetch origin in @apostrophecms/ai-helper, enabling authenticated SSRF
items.summary: ## Summary The `@apostrophecms/ai-helper` package builds the URL for a server-side image fetch by resolving a storage-relative path against `req.baseUrl`. items.summary: A denial of service (DoS) vulnerability was identified in `@angular/router` when Server-Side Rendering (SSR) is enabled on Node.js (V8). items.title: Crass : Large numeric exponents cause CPU and memory denial of service
items.summary: ### Impact Crass converts CSS scientific notation number values with unbounded exponentiation before it clamps the result to `Float::MAX`. Applications that use Crass to parse attacker-controlled CSS strings can be forced to spend disproportionate CPU and memory parsing a tiny input, possibly resulting in a crash. ### Patches This is fixed in Crass 1.0.7. ### Related - https://github.com/rubysec/ruby-advisory-db/blob/master/gems/crass/GHSA-6wmf-3r64-vcwv.yml
